patterns.rule: Drop the **-a** and add **-ar** (tala → talar) or **-er** (läsa → läser). A stem that already ends in **-r** adds nothing (höra → hör). Every person takes the same form.
patterns.subtitle: Swedish verbs in -a: one form for all six persons, ending in -r.

patterns.rule: Verbs that end in a long vowel just add **-r** (bo → bor, tro → tror). Every person takes the same form.
patterns.subtitle: Short Swedish verbs in a vowel: add -r.

patterns.rule: Verbs that end in **-å** just add **-r** (gå → går, stå → står). Every person takes the same form.
patterns.subtitle: Short Swedish verbs in -å: add -r.

concepts.label: Samordnande
concepts.labelGloss: joins two main clauses; both keep normal word order (och, men, eller, för, så, utan)
concepts.explainer:
A **samordnande konjunktion** joins two main clauses, each of which could stand alone. After it, the second clause keeps **normal word order**: the subject first, then the verb.

There are only six. Learn them by heart, because every other conjunction works differently:

**och · men · eller · för · så · utan**

| Clause 1 | | Clause 2, normal order |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jag är hungrig, | **och** | jag **vill** äta nu. |
| Det regnar, | **men** | vi **går** ut ändå. |
| Hon är inte trött, | **utan** | hon **är** hungrig. |

> The conjunction stands *outside* the clause. Read what follows it as a sentence of its own: *vi går ut ändå*.

**För** means *because* and always comes second, after a comma: *Jag stannar hemma, för jag är sjuk.* **Så** (so) can be a conjunction, *så vi tog bussen*, or an adverb that pulls the verb forward, *så tog vi bussen*. Both are correct.

**Utan** is the *but* that follows a **negative**: *inte i dag, utan i morgon* (not today but tomorrow).

:::order{sentence="Jag tar en taxi, för bussen har redan gått." after="för" en="I'm taking a taxi, because the bus has already left."}
:::

concepts.label: Underordnande
concepts.labelGloss: starts a bisats; inte goes before the verb (att, när, om, eftersom, fastän)
concepts.explainer:
An **underordnande konjunktion** starts a **bisats**, a clause that can't stand on its own. Inside it the verb stays right after the subject, as in English. But **inte**, **aldrig**, **alltid** and other short adverbs move *in front of* the verb.

**att · när · om** *(if, whether)* **· eftersom · fastän · medan · innan · tills · därför att · så att**

| Main clause | | Bisats |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jag är trött | **eftersom** | jag **inte** sov i natt. |
| Jag vet | **att** | han **alltid** kommer sent. |
| Vi går ut | **om** | det **inte** regnar. |

In a main clause, *inte* comes after the verb: *jag sov inte*. In a bisats it comes before it: *eftersom jag inte sov*. Swedish teachers call this **BIFF**: *i **b**isats **i**nte **f**öre **f**initum*, "in a subordinate clause, inte before the finite verb".

When the bisats comes first, it takes the first place of the sentence, so the main clause starts with its verb:

***Eftersom** det är sent **går** vi hem.*

> **För or eftersom?** Both mean *because*. **För** joins two main clauses: *för jag är trött*. **Eftersom** starts a bisats and can open the sentence: *Eftersom jag är trött...*

:::order{sentence="Vi stannar inne eftersom det inte slutar regna." after="eftersom" en="We're staying in because it won't stop raining."}
:::
